MCCCOMM212.contribution: Climate communication, protest art and public debate directly support cultural perspectives on climate.

analysis: The strongest provisional response combines cultural history, literary and visual interpretation, philosophy, media and qualitative research. Identity and inclusion can draw directly on gender history, art restitution, media and race, and stigma and othering. Heritage could combine curatorial and material media study with technical database methods; an integrated archive digitisation sequence is limited. Technology and media have direct coverage in media archaeology and AI ethics. Health stigma has sociological and cultural narrative coverage, while clinical psychology alone would not make it a cultural-studies direction. These are contribution findings only. Final concepts, placements and distinctness depend on the external allocation.
